data.name: MESSAGE_PORTAL_PRIVACY.Text
data.value:
The French version of this page is the authoritative version.

Privacy Statement for the site:

[Portal:PortalName]

Date of last update: 30/01/2005

On the site [Portal:PortalName] (hereinafter referred to as the “Site”), we are committed to protecting your personal data. This privacy statement applies solely to this site; it cannot apply to other sites, whether online or offline, nor to other products or services. By accessing the Site, you accept the recording of your information and the terms of use described in this privacy statement.

On this page

  • Collection of your personal information

  • Use of your personal data

  • Control of your personal information

  • Access to your personal data

  • Security of your personal information

  • Protection of children’s personal information

  • Cookies

  • Enforcement of this privacy statement

  • Changes to this privacy statement

  • Contacts

Collection of your personal information

We will ask you for information when we need data that personally identifies you (personal information) or that allows us to contact you. Generally, such information is required when we provide you with a service or carry out a transaction that you have requested, for example for information on the products and services of this Site, entry into a contest, subscription to e-mail newsletters, access to a priority site with restricted access, or the purchase and registration of products on this Site. The personal information we collect may include your name, your job title, the name of your company or organization, your business e-mail address, your business telephone number, your business or home postal address, information about your position or your company, and credit card information.

The Site may also collect information about your visit, including the name of your Internet service provider and the IP address used to access the Internet, the date and time of access to the site, the pages you access on the Site, and the URL of the site from which you arrived at our site. This information is intended for trend analysis and for the administration and improvement of the Site.

In order to prevent your e-mail address or other personal information from being harvested and misused by others, we recommend that you exercise caution in using an existing e-mail address or other personal information in newsgroups, chats or other public forums.

Top of page

Use of your personal data

The personal information collected on this Site is used for the operation of the Site and to enable us to provide you with the service or to complete the transaction that you have requested or authorized.

In the context of these uses, this Site may use personal information in order to provide you with more effective customer service, to improve the Site and any other product or service of this Site, and to make browsing easier for you by sparing you from entering the same information several times or by tailoring the site to your preferences or interests. In order to offer you a consistent environment in your interactions with our Site, the information collected may be used in combination with information collected by other services of our Site.

We may use your personal information to send you important information about the product or service you are using.

We combine site visit data with anonymous demographic data for research purposes; the resulting volumes of information are used so as to provide you with the content you expect. In certain restricted-access areas of our Site, with your consent, we will combine site visit data with your personal data in order to offer you personalized content. Without your authorization, we will not be able to provide you with a personalized service and we will not be able to combine your personal data with site visit data.

When you subscribe to a newsletter or indicate that you wish to receive promotional e-mail messages, our Site may use personalized links or other similar technologies to track the links you click in e-mail messages. We may associate this information with your personal information in order to send you even more targeted messages or information.

Certain services on our Site offer individuals the possibility of publicly displaying certain personal information, for example for one of our partners who wishes to publish its contact information in connection with the services it offers. Participation in such services is always optional.

Our Site sometimes uses other companies to provide certain services on its behalf. These may include, for example, website hosting, the packaging, shipping and delivery of prizes, answering customer questions about products and services, or sending information about our products, special offers or other new services. We will provide these companies only with the personal information necessary for their service. These companies are required to maintain the confidentiality of such information and may under no circumstances use it for any other purpose.

We will disclose your personal information only if required by law or if we believe in good faith that such action is necessary to comply with legal enactments or legal process, to protect and defend our rights or property, and to act in emergencies to protect the personal safety of our employees and users of the site.

Personal information collected on the Site may be stored and used in France or in any other country in which its subsidiaries, partners or agents are present. By using the Site, you consent to such transfers of your personal information outside your country.

We respect and comply with the Act of 6 January 1978 (link to the CNIL website).

Top of page

Control of your personal information

Except as otherwise stated in this statement, the personal information you provide on the Site will not be transferred outside its subsidiaries and partners without your authorization. As described in the following section, you may access your personal information and choose how you wish to be contacted.

This privacy statement and the choices you make on the Site do not necessarily apply to personal information that you have provided to us in the context of other, separate products or services.

We may periodically send you e-mails to inform you of technical service or security issues relating to a product or service you have requested, or to acknowledge receipt of a request for a product or service. In certain services offered on our Site, contact with the customer is an essential element of the service. You will not be able to unsubscribe from these mailings, as they form an integral part of the service you have chosen.

Top of page

Access to your personal data

You may rectify your personal data and your contact information on this Site after logging in.

Certain services we offer may collect information that is not accessible through your personal settings. However, in such cases, you may access your personal data by contacting us as explained at the bottom of this statement, or through other means of communication described by the service.

Top of page

Security of your personal information

We rigorously guarantee the protection of your personal information. We use a variety of security technologies and procedures to ensure the protection of your personal data and to prevent it from being accessed, used or disclosed without authorization. For example, we store the data you provide to us on servers with restricted access located in monitored facilities. In addition, when we transmit sensitive confidential information over the Internet (a credit card number, for example), such information is protected by means of an encryption system such as the SSL (Secure Socket Layer) protocol or any other technique enabling the encryption of such information.

Top of page

Protection of children’s personal information

Our Site does not knowingly collect personal information from children.

Top of page

Cookies

Cookies are used on this Site to ensure the integrity of the registration process and to personalize the Site. A cookie is a small text file placed on your hard disk by a Web page server. It cannot be used to run programs or to infect your computer with viruses. Cookies are assigned exclusively to you and can be read only by the Web servers belonging to the domain that issued the cookie to you.

One of the main practical functions of cookies is to save you time. For example, if you personalize a Web page or navigate within a site, the cookie will help the site retrieve your specific information on subsequent visits. This makes it possible, in particular, to simplify the process of delivering content of interest to you and navigation on the site. When you return to the site, the information you previously provided is reused to allow you to use more easily the site features that you have personalized.

We may also use invisible pixels, also known as clear GIFs, to assist in placing the cookie. We use this technology as a tool for compiling statistics on the use of our Site. These statistics include the number of visitors who clicked on key elements (for example, links or graphics) of a Web page, a Web log page or a newsletter of our Site. We may share compiled statistics with partner companies, but we do not authorize other companies to place .gif images or cookies on our sites, except in the case of a particular temporary interest for our customers (for example, through the integration of a service from a site based on third-party cookies or clear .gifs).

You may accept or refuse cookies. Most Web browsers accept cookies automatically, but you may change your browser settings to deny them access to your computer if you so wish. If you choose to refuse cookies, you may not be able to use fully the interactive features of this site or of other websites you visit.

Top of page

Enforcement of this privacy statement

If you have any questions regarding this statement, please contact us using the form we make available to you, which you can access after logging in.

Top of page

Changes to this privacy statement

We occasionally update this privacy statement. In such cases, we also revise the “last updated” date at the top of the privacy statement. In the event of material changes to this statement, we will inform you by posting a prominent notice on the site’s home page or by sending you a notification directly. We encourage you to review this privacy statement regularly in order to stay informed of how we help protect the personal information we collect. Continued use of this service constitutes your acceptance of this privacy statement and of its updates.

Top of page

Contacts

Your comments regarding this privacy statement are welcome. If you believe that our Site has not complied with this privacy statement, please contact us electronically or by post at the address set out in the terms of use, and we will use all reasonable means to promptly identify and remedy the problem.

Top of page

data.name: 404.Error
data.value:
Domain Name {0} Does Not Exist In The Database

This system supports multiple websites from a single database/codebase. It accomplishes this by converting the URL of the client browser request to a valid Portal row in the Portals database table. The following steps describe the process:

  1. Web Server Processing
    • When a web server receives a request from a client browser, it compares the file name extension on the target URL resource to its Application Extension Mappings defined in IIS.
    • Based on the corresponding match, IIS then sends the request to the defined Executable Path (aspnet_asapi.dll in the case of ASP.NET requests).
    • The aspnet_isapi.dll engine processes the request in an ordered series of events beginning with Application_BeginRequest.
  2. HttpModule.URLRewrite OnBeginRequest (UrlRewriteModule.vb)
    • The request URL is parsed based on the "/" character
    • A domain name is constructed using each of the relevant parsed URL segments.

      Examples:
      URL: https://www.domain.com/default.aspx = Domain Name: www.domain.com
      URL: https://209.75.24.131/default.aspx = Domain Name: 209.75.24.131
      URL: https://localhost/DotNetNuke/default.aspx = Domain Name: localhost/DotNetNuke
      URL: https://www.domain.com/virtualdirectory/default.aspx = Domain Name: www.domain.com/virtualdirectory
      URL: https://www.domain.com/directory/default.aspx = Domain Name: www.domain.com/directory

    • Using the domain name, the application queries the database ( PortalAlias table - column HTTTPAlias) to locate a matching record.

      Note: If you are installing the application to a remote server you must modify the HTTPAlias field value in table PortalAlias for the record with proper PortalID, according to the rules defined above.

data.name: 403_3.Error
data.value:
DNN Configuration Error

{0}

Your DNN installation appears to have a security settings problem (most likely permissions). DNN has extensive file upload capabilities for content, modules, and themes. These features require custom security settings so that the application is able to create and remove files in your website.

On your webserver, browse to the root folder of the website (C:\DotNetNuke by default) using Windows Explorer. Right-click the folder and select "Sharing and Security" from the popup menu. Select tab "Security". Add the appropriate user account and set proper permissions for the ASP.Net user, specified in advanced setting of the IIS application pool that is hosting your website.

  • If using a named account like builtin "NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE"
    1. The user Account must be granted Read, Write, Read & Execute, and Modify permission.

  • If using "ApplicationPoolIdentity" (recommended)
    1. User account IIS AppPool\[AppPool Name] (replace [AppPool Name] by the real name of the IIS application pool) must be granted Read, Write, Read & Execute, and Modify permission.
